audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal is called her ultimate five times: spikes[2].when literally reads 'Mel R', spikes[2].text says 'Mel's Reflect (R)', mid says 'Track her R cooldown — if she has not burned Reflect recently', late says 'her R Reflect can bounce damage back in 5v5', whys[6] and wants.foe[2] repeat it. Her actual ultimate, Golden Eclipse, is never mentioned once.
audit.why: Rebuttal is her W. The distinction is not cosmetic — the player is being told to track a 120/100/80 ultimate when the ability they mean is on 38/35/33/29/26 with a mana cost that falls from 80 to zero. At rank 1 that is the longest cooldown in her kit and a genuine window; at rank 5 it is free and back every 26 seconds. It also does more than reflect: it 'prevents her from taking damage' and grants her move speed, so committing into it wastes the whole pattern, not just a projectile.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal is her W: 38s at rank 1 falling to 26s, free at rank 5. It reflects projectiles, blanks her damage intake and speeds her up. Bait it with one auto, then commit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W Rebuttal, cd 38/35/33/29/26, cost 80/60/40/20/0; R Golden Eclipse, cd 120/100/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: Searing Brilliance and Overwhelm are absent from both layers, and Golden Eclipse appears nowhere at all.
audit.why: These two are one mechanic and it is the reason this lane is dangerous in a way the entry never explains. Every time Mel deals damage with an ability or an attack she applies Overwhelm, the stacks accumulate without limit, and enough Overwhelm damage consumes the stacks to execute the target. Golden Eclipse then 'strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her' — a global cast at 25000 range, dealing more per stack. So the chip Trundle is told to eat is building an execute, and walking out of lane at low health with stacks on is not safety. It is also 120/100/80, the same timer as Subjugate.
audit.corrected: Every ability and attack of hers stacks Overwhelm on you, and enough of it executes. Golden Eclipse is global and hits everyone still carrying stacks, on 120/100/80 — the same timer as Subjugate.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (P Searing Brilliance, execute; R Golden Eclipse, range 25000, cd 120/100/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp is credited with an attack-speed effect three times: early says 'your AS steal degrades her subsequent autos', mid says 'Q-bite to steal her AD and slow her attack speed', wants.you[0] says 'Chomp's AS-steal'. mid also refers to 'her W/E burst'.
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and briefly slows movement — there is no attack-speed component in Trundle's kit except Frozen Domain's buff on himself. And 'W/E burst' is wrong on the W half: Rebuttal is a defensive barrier, so her damage comes from Radiant Volley, Solar Snare, Golden Eclipse and her attacks, not from W.
audit.corrected: Chomp saps Attack Damage on a flat 3.5s. Her damage is Radiant Volley, Solar Snare and her empowered attacks — Rebuttal is purely defensive.

audit.whatIsWrong: No ability in either kit carries a cooldown or a range anywhere in this entry. whys[1] does not even name what she has at level 2 — 'her zone or execute tool'. breakdown.cooldowns says 'Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it.'
audit.why: The ranges are the lane. Radiant Volley reaches 950 and Solar Snare 1000 against Chomp's 300, which is why the walk-up is the whole problem — and Radiant Volley's 10/9/8/7/6 is the window when it whiffs. Solar Snare is also more forgiving than 'dodge it' suggests: it 'roots those at its center while the area around it slows', so stepping toward the edge downgrades a root into a slow, which is a survivable outcome rather than a lost trade.
audit.corrected: Radiant Volley 950 range on 10s at rank 1; Solar Snare 1000 range on 11s, rooting only at its centre with a slowing ring around it. Chomp answers at 300.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (Q cd 10/9/8/7/6 range 950; E cd 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 range 1000)

edits.before: Level 1 is a coin flip — Mel has ranged Q poke and you have melee Chomp, so you trade a bite for a poke every time you step up for last hits. Accept small chip damage if you land Chomp, because you immediately heal part of it back from King's Tribute on dying minions. The danger window is level 2: Mel adds her zone or execute tool before you have Frozen Domain or Pillar, meaning she can poke you down in the opening minutes without a clean escape for you. Keep the wave tight to your side, walk up only when she is casting, and look for a single Chomp on her while she goes for CS — your AS steal degrades her subsequent autos even in these short pokes.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coin flip — Mel pokes with Radiant Volley from 950 while you answer at 300, so you trade a bite for a poke every time you step up for last hits. Accept the chip when Chomp lands, because King's Tribute heals part of it back off dying minions. The danger window is level 2: she adds Solar Snare before you have Frozen Domain or Pillar, and every hit she lands stacks Overwhelm on you — enough of it executes, so this chip is not just chip. Keep the wave tight to your side, walk up while she is casting, and take a single Chomp while she goes for CS; the AD it saps weakens her follow-up autos.

edits.before: At level 3 your entire kit is live: place Frozen Domain on yourself the instant she commits to a trade, Pillar her retreat path, and Q-bite to steal her AD and slow her attack speed. Inside your domain you move faster, attack faster, and heal continuously — a ranged mage who cannot kite has no answer to this pattern. Level 6 is your clearest swing: Subjugate mid-fight drains a chunk of her Magic Resistance directly onto you, which softens every subsequent W/E burst she throws. Open R as soon as the all-in starts so the stolen resists are live for the entire exchange. Track her R cooldown — if she has not burned Reflect recently, do not dump all your burst at once; bait it with an auto or a Pillar cast first, then commit the real kill pattern once it is gone.
edits.after: At level 3 your entire kit is live: place Frozen Domain on yourself the instant she commits, Pillar her retreat path, and Q-bite every 3.5s to sap her AD. Inside your domain you move faster, attack faster and heal continuously — a ranged mage who cannot kite has no answer to that. Level 6 is your clearest swing: Subjugate takes Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft over four seconds, and the Magic Resist you wear softens everything she throws. Open R as the all-in starts. The cooldown to track is Rebuttal — her W, not her ultimate — at 38s at rank 1, and while it holds she takes no damage at all. Bait it with an auto or a Pillar cast, then commit the real kill pattern once it is spent.

edits.before: With two items Trundle is too durable and too sticky for Mel to duel in a side lane — Subjugate's resistance drain plus Frozen Domain movement means you can close any gap she creates with her zoning spells. She becomes a team-fight problem rather than a lane problem: her R Reflect can bounce damage back in 5v5 chaos, so do not open with your hardest hitting combo in a teamfight; auto-Chomp first to bait the reflect timer, then dump everything once it is spent. Your carry ceiling scales with how tanky her team is — if she is the only AP threat, your Subjugate payoff is modest, but if their front line is armored up you remain a dominant stat-drain engine through the whole game.
edits.after: With two items Trundle is too durable and too sticky for Mel to duel in a side lane — Subjugate's theft plus Frozen Domain movement closes any gap her zoning creates. She becomes a team-fight problem instead: Rebuttal (W) reflects projectiles and blanks her damage intake, so open with an auto and a Chomp to bait it rather than your whole pattern, then commit once it is spent. Golden Eclipse is the other half — it is global and strikes everyone still carrying Overwhelm stacks, so leaving a fight at low health is not the same as being safe. Your ceiling still scales with how armoured their front line is, since that is what Subjugate takes.

notes: BIGGEST CORRECTION: the entry calls Rebuttal her ultimate in five separate strings, including spikes[2].when which literally reads 'Mel R'. Rebuttal is her W, on 38/35/33/29/26 with a mana cost falling from 80 to zero — so the player was told to track a 120-second timer for an ability that is back every 26 seconds and free at max rank. It also does more than reflect: it prevents her taking damage and grants move speed, which is why committing into it wastes the entire pattern. BIGGEST ADD: Searing Brilliance, Overwhelm and Golden Eclipse were absent from both layers. Any ability or attack of hers stacks Overwhelm without limit, enough Overwhelm executes the target, and Golden Eclipse is a global cast at 25000 range that strikes everyone still carrying stacks and scales with them. That changes the entry's core instruction — it repeatedly tells the player to accept chip, when the chip is assembling an execute and following them out of lane. Golden Eclipse is also 120/100/80, the same timer as Subjugate. CORRECTED: Chomp credited with an attack-speed effect in three strings; it saps Attack Damage and briefly slows. Also 'her W/E burst' — W is defensive. ADDED RANGES: Radiant Volley 950 on 10s, Solar Snare 1000 on 11s, against Chomp's 300 — the range gap is the lane, and no string had a number in it. Solar Snare also roots only at its centre with a slowing ring around, so 'dodge it' becomes the more useful 'step toward the edge'. FIXED: tldr, winCon, report[0].t, report[1].t and dontsFull[2].t all call Mel 'him'. NOT EDITED (enum): the chart gives Trundle zero of seven stages in a 53.64% lane the full layer calls FAV, while the prose calls Level 6 'your clearest swing' and says she cannot duel you at two items — win[4] and win[6] should read Trundle. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: whether Rebuttal reflects anything in Trundle's kit. Chomp is a targeted bite and Pillar of Ice is a ground-targeted terrain cast, so neither reads as a projectile, but Riot's text does not define what counts and the kit files' needsResearch blocks are empty — I described the damage-immunity half, which is the part that decides the trade, and made no claim about reflection either way.
